Root cause was Serve() binding inside the caller's goroutine, so socket-exists lagged goroutine-started. Root cause was not the go-run shim: main had 'defer ctl.stop()' followed by os.Exit(1) on a failing suite, and os.Exit does not run defers — so cleanup ran on success and was skipped on failure, the common case. main is now a wrapper around run() int, plus a signal handler for Ctrl-C. Measured, since a passing run proves nothing here (it exits 0, where the old code was already fine). Failing suite with the broker alive: old exit=1 leaked 2 brokers + 1 temp dir; new exit=1 leaked 0 and 0. Clean run still 41/41, exit=0, 0 leaked.

Fixed by resync-at-quote-time rather than the rejection-inference approach the bead proposed. The payee reports highest_seen_nonce/has_seen_nonces in GetTicketParamsResponse; the broker relays them; the payer raises its durable watermark to match before signing anything. A lost counter heals on the next quote at no cost, instead of costing a refused payment first — and a duplicate delivery still reports NONCE_REPLAY without rotating the route, because nothing is being inferred from the rejection at all.

Every enrollment-scoped route authenticated with the enrollment bearer token, and lnm-6at.7 had just made the agent rotate that token every 24h — so any browser copy would die within a day by design, with recovery meaning reading a token off the host by hand. Committed 1e4a472. NOT DONE, and it blocks a real deployment: the five curated templates ship with runner_compose empty (lnm-v12), so a pool cannot actually start a runner from the catalog. Committed c907893. Resolved as option (b) with the guard kept: refusing the second claim is what stops a challenger taking an incumbent's card contested by declaring its uuid, so the incumbent keeps it and the REFUSAL is recorded. That matches 0040 §4.2 — the challenger's card does not activate, the incumbent's is untouched.

The queue was reading duplicate HardwareUnit rows, which the guard guarantees can never exist. New types.HardwareClaimConflict, upserted on (gpu, challenger) so a host re-attaching every 30s is one dispute seen repeatedly. RelayHardware already computed conflicts and the relay loop printed them to stderr and dropped them; they are now persisted.

Two operator resolutions, both requiring a reason: transfer (retire the incumbent's unit so the challenger's next attach succeeds — it stops refusing rather than handing the card over) and reject. A rejected dispute that recurs is REOPENED, because a host still trying after a rejection is new information. Documented in RUNBOOK.md.

Committed c907893. POST /admin/v1/template-assignments/{id}/reinstate, defaulting to certification_testing rather than probationary: the failures that cause suspension are exactly what certification tests, re-proving costs one automated probe, and the ladder promotes from there on its own. {"to":"probationary_real_traffic"} is available for a placement suspended by mistake. Reason required.

THE TRAP THIS BEAD FLAGGED WAS REAL AND WORSE THAN RECORDED: the ladder counted certification failures over ALL runs, unbounded, so a placement suspended after two failures would have been re-suspended by the same historical count on the very next tick — the operator's decision undoing itself once a minute, indefinitely. types.TemplateAssignment.ReinstatedAt is now the boundary evidence is counted from; history is kept rather than reset. Unit test on the boundary plus an end-to-end guard (suspend via ladder -> reinstate -> next RunOnce produces no transition).

Selection state handled in both directions as the bead required: probationary is eligible with a real MaxShareCap AND probation's concurrency cap (eligible-with-zero reads to the broker as UNCAPPED); certification_testing stays excluded with reason awaiting_recertification. A missing selection row is seeded here rather than skipped — leaving it to the ladder's next pass would create the eligible-and-uncapped row this exists to prevent.

Also refused: reinstating a placement whose MEMBER is suspended (409). Returning work to someone the pool has stopped dealing with should not fall out of a per-placement gesture.

Fixed in aeef514. The test pinned exact template ids, which made it a test of which products the pool sold that week — it broke on the catalog rebuild and would have broken again on the next price change. It now asserts the STANCE from 0040 §4.4: older classes run one workload, 4090/5090 run a primary plus at most one rider, and any rider must both declare that class in stacking.secondary_on and carry a capacity.max_in_flight (or 'low-footprint' is a word in a plan rather than a property). Added a second test catching a template that offers to ride on a class its own requirements exclude. Took the subagent's recommendation to test the property rather than the capability id.

Fixed in capability-broker/internal/credentialstore: syncExpiry gives a zero-expiry sync entry the store's DefaultExpiry, clamps a pool-supplied expiry to MaxExpiry, and leaves an existing expiry alone on re-push. Four unit tests plus the e2e harness, verified red without the fix.

Built: e2e/ module with harness.go (boots both binaries, free ports, generated configs, process-group cleanup), runner.go (fake runner speaking the attach tunnel), member.go (SIWE sign-in, enrol, hardware, desired state), catalog.go (fixture + shipped catalog), and two tests. Both green; found lnm-8wv on the first run.

Built the certification usage tap. certification/usagetap.go mints a per-run callback (id + bearer token, token stored only as a hash) that the session step hands the runner as callback_url/callback_token at create; the runner reports to it exactly as it reports to a paid session's callback, since the URL is opaque to it. New broker route POST /internal/v1/certification/usage/{tap_id} ingests the same event envelope as the paid surface and records nothing else — no session record, no debit. The usage step now waits window_ms (spec default 10000) for the report, then judges it: silence fails, a unit other than the declared work_unit fails, a shortfall against min_units fails, and evidence carries work_unit/units/event_at per certification-steps §3.3. Taps are closed by the run that opened them and swept if abandoned.

Covered by 15 unit tests plus two e2e tests that post the usage report over real HTTP to whatever URL the broker put in the create body — the seam where a wrong external_base_url, an unregistered route, or a token that does not verify all look identical from inside either service.

Also updated the two shipped session templates whose comments documented this gap; video-transcode-live's usage step stays optional for the workload reason (it meters OUTPUT seconds and a certification session has no publisher), which is now the only reason.

Decided to validate now rather than wait: the placement engine (lnm-6at.4) has landed, so the manual route is an override rather than the only way to assign, and an override checked by a different rule than the planner is worse than none.

placement.Validate is the shared gate — it calls the planner's own requirementsFail, placeable, and stackableOn rather than restating them, and a test asserts Plan and Validate agree on the same pairing. The route now rejects: a template not in the catalog, a hardware unit that does not exist, a card whose class/model/VRAM fails the template's requirements, a card that is suspended or retired, a secondary role on a template that does not declare that class in stacking.secondary_on, a primary role on a template that does not declare stacking.primary, an unrecognised role, and a missing id on either side.

Deliberately NOT checked: stacking limits per class, priority order, member opt-outs. Those are pool preference and overriding a preference is the point of an override; a card that physically cannot run the workload is not a preference.

The route also now derives host_enrollment_id and member_eth_address from the hardware unit instead of trusting the body (a disagreement there would send desired state to the wrong machine and earnings to the wrong wallet), defaults the id to the planner's <unit>|<template> so a hand-written and a planned assignment for one pair are one record, and appends an audit event as plan/apply already does.

Found and fixed alongside: all three routes calling deps.RefreshRendered panicked when that callback was nil — a nil-pointer dereference in a handler goroutine, so the operator saw a dropped connection rather than an error. Now routed through a Deps.refresh method that no-ops.

9 new tests across internal/placement and internal/server/admin.

Fixed in capability-broker/internal/server/attach.go: both transports now call runners.Attach before sending register_result, and onRunnerAttached after it. Pinned by TestAttachIsVisibleTheInstantItIsAcknowledged. The e2e fake runner was restructured to a single reader as a consequence.

Deleted. Broker: internal/workerconn/registry.go (Registry, Forwarder, HTTPTransport, registryTransport) and its two test files; RegisterBackendIDs/RegisterAuthorization; the legacy branch of the QUIC listener; requireWorkerSessionAuth and the backend_ids query on the attach path; GET/POST /admin/v1/worker-sessions*. Controller: Deps.KillWorkerSession, killEnrollmentAssignments, brokeradmin.Client.KillWorkerSession, and the dead Listen.WorkerQUIC config the controller parsed and never used.

Two findings the deletion turned up:

1. The controller's revoke route called KillWorkerSession(assignment.ID) against a registry keyed by worker backend ids, so it unregistered nothing and reported killed_worker_sessions that were never killed. Worse, the route did not push, so revoking a host left its credential valid on the broker and the runner attached and earning until someone happened to reload. Revoke now pushes ('host-enrollment-revoked'); the broker revokes the credential and closes every connection holding it, and a failed push is reported as broker_push_error rather than swallowed.

2. listen.worker_quic could NOT be deleted as the bead assumed: the same listener carries runner attach over QUIC, and its address goes into every member bundle. Renamed to listen.attach_quic, with worker_quic still read and a deprecation warning at load, since silently ceasing to listen for attaches is the worst possible upgrade behaviour. The WebSocket path /internal/v1/worker/session keeps its spelling for the same reason.

Kept, as the bead specified: TunnelMessage, ReadRegister, IsAttachRegister, AcceptQUICRegister, SessionForwarder, QUICSessionForwarder — all attach machinery.

Docs swept: capability-broker/README.md, and protocols/broker-admin.md bumped to 1.1.0-draft with a changelog row recording the removal (1.0.0-draft had already marked the routes superseded; they are now gone).
